correctness.rationale: Exact regenerative equations hold at each fresh state entry. The finite transient Green matrix N is nonnegative and finite, giving m=Nmu and second moment N(nu+2a). The classical sharp rearrangement bound applies since m_destination is bounded and holding means are finite. Its quantile upper/lower couplings attain every a_i extremum; independent rowwise choice realizes simultaneous bounds for every start. Mixing kernels interpolates the full attainable variance interval. Strictness follows when a nonconstant holding law and a nonconstant residual-mean destination law coexist at a reachable state. A continuous three-state example is integrated exactly and 1954 exact rational assertions over 216 couplings corroborate finite models; the analytical argument, not these finite checks, proves the theorem.

value.rationale: This is a natural model-identification and network-reliability variance question: transition rows and per-state holding-time marginals are often observed while their destination-duration dependence is not. The theorem gives exact computable sharp uncertainty bounds for every starting state without optimizing path distributions, identifies extremal dependence policies and strictness under graph reachability, and realizes a thirteen-fold change in exact variance without altering any prescribed marginal or first moment. It neither claims higher-order stochastic order nor relies on an arbitrary selected numerical invariant.
